fixFirst.title: OS command execution
fixFirst.what: The code launches an operating-system command or shell.
fixFirst.why: If any part of the command is built from untrusted input, an attacker can add commands of their own (command injection).
fixFirst.fix: Avoid popen(). Use a library API, or exec-family calls with an argument array and validated input.
fixFirst.caveat: The analyser cannot see where the arguments come from; fixed commands are lower risk.

fixFirst.title: Very long function
fixFirst.what: A function or method is longer than 100 lines.
fixFirst.why: Long functions are hard to read, test and change safely, and they tend to collect bugs.
fixFirst.fix: Split it into smaller functions that each do one job.

fixFirst.title: Deeply nested code
fixFirst.what: A file reaches a nesting depth greater than 6 (ifs, loops and blocks inside each other).
fixFirst.why: Each extra level of nesting makes the logic harder to follow and test.
fixFirst.fix: Use early returns, extract helper functions, and flatten conditions.

fixFirst.title: Empty error handler
fixFirst.what: A catch block does nothing with the caught error.
fixFirst.why: Failures vanish silently, so bugs surface later, far from their cause, and are hard to diagnose.
fixFirst.fix: Log the error, handle it meaningfully, or re-throw it. If ignoring it is intentional, add a comment saying why.

fixFirst.title: Manual new/delete
fixFirst.what: The code uses raw new or delete instead of a smart pointer or container.
fixFirst.why: Forgetting a delete leaks memory; deleting twice or on an early return causes crashes.
fixFirst.fix: Use std::make_unique / std::make_shared or an RAII container such as std::vector.
